data: Russia's GNSS — 24 sats, restored to full coverage in 2011
Roscosmos GLONASS programme. First launched 1982; collapsed in the 1990s post-Soviet funding crisis; restored to 24-satellite operational status 2011.

Russia's GNSS — 24 active satellites at 19,130 km MEO in 3 planes inclined 64.8° (the high inclination is deliberate for better high-latitude coverage relative to GPS). First launched 1982; reached full constellation in 1995, then collapsed in the late 1990s / early 2000s after Soviet funding ended; restored to full 24-satellite operational status around 2010-2011 with funding revival. Continues operational in 2026. Operated by Roscosmos in coordination with the Russian Ministry of Defence.
Russian 12-hour HEO comms — 63.4° critical inclination locks apogee over the north

Russia's global navigation system. Designed during the Cold War, launched 1982. Uses a higher inclination than GPS — better coverage of polar regions. Russia opened it to civilian use in 2007.
